what_happened: In job 7qht, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a request. Criterion 5 in that reading was a behavior criterion with a recorded check (fmt, clippy, test) as its evidence. The current decision D43 rejects that pairing. The user changed criterion 5 into a content criterion that is met by Athena's own recorded fmt, clippy and test checks on the candidate. The rest of the reading stayed. The correction came before the work went on.
cause: Athena builds criteria from the request text and does not test each one against the decisions that govern how criteria are judged. D43 says what kind of evidence a behavior criterion may use. Nothing makes the reading stage check a criterion's type against its evidence, so a mismatch passes until the user spots it. The registry class also shows the same gap for other defaults and invariants.
prevention: Add a check at reading acceptance. For every criterion it reads the declared type (behavior or content) and the named evidence. It compares them with the rules from D43 and the other criterion-judging defaults. It rejects a reading, with the criterion named, when a behavior criterion relies on a recorded check as its only evidence. The reading stage then fixes the type or the evidence before the user sees the reading. The rules the check uses are written as data in one place, so a decision change updates the check.
proposed_request: Add a check to the reading-acceptance step. For each acceptance criterion in a reading, compare its type (behavior or content) with its stated evidence under the current D43 and the other decisions about criterion evidence. Reject the reading and name the criterion when a behavior criterion has a recorded check (fmt, clippy or test) as its only evidence. Keep the rules in one data file that cites the decision ids. Add tests with a passing reading, a rejected reading, and a reading where a content criterion is met by a recorded check. Add a CHANGELOG entry. Run the full test suite at most once.
